title: HNSW Vector Database from Scratch with Cosine Similarity, Multi-Layer Graph Index & REST API
problem: Modern generative AI systems and Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) pipelines rely fundamentally on high-recall, low-latency vector similarity search across high-dimensional embeddings. Off-the-shelf commercial vector databases (e.g. Pinecone, Weaviate) are expensive managed cloud services that function as opaque black boxes, hiding algorithmic indexing bottlenecks, memory consumption profiles, and recall-latency tradeoffs. Furthermore, naive flat brute-force search scales with O(N) linear complexity, becoming computationally unusable beyond modest vector counts. This project builds a production-grade HNSW (Hierarchical Navigable Small World) vector database from scratch in Python and NumPy without third-party vector search libraries. The engine constructs a multi-layer proximity graph with configurable connection parameters (M) and construction beam widths (ef_construction), implements greedy search with heuristic pruning, achieves >= 95% Recall@10 against exact brute-force search on 100,000 vectors, serializes graph indices to disk, and exposes a high-concurrency FastAPI query interface with sub-6ms search latency.

use_cases.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) Semantic Document Retrieval
use_cases.first_sentence: Enterprise knowledge base chatbots querying millions of document text chunk embeddings must retrieve the top-10 most semantically relevant contexts in milliseconds.
use_cases.second_sentence: The custom HNSW index traverses hierarchical graph layers via cosine distance, returning top-10 nearest chunk vectors with over 95% recall compared to brute-force search.

use_cases.title: E-Commerce Semantic Product Visual Similarity Search
use_cases.first_sentence: Online retail platforms allowing customers to search for visually similar fashion items via deep learning image embeddings need low-latency catalog indexing.
use_cases.second_sentence: The engine constructs multi-layer proximity graphs over 100,000 image feature vectors, enabling sub-6ms nearest neighbor lookups during peak traffic.

use_cases.title: Real-Time Facial Recognition Identity Matching Engine
use_cases.first_sentence: Security systems matching live camera video face embeddings against authorized employee databases require deterministic nearest neighbor ranking.
use_cases.second_sentence: The vector database serializes binary graph structures to disk and provides instant warm-restart index loading without re-indexing raw vector corpora.

hard_parts: Implementing the multi-layer HNSW graph construction algorithm with exponential layer decay probabilities and heuristic neighbor selection in pure Python/NumPy
Optimizing beam search traversal across upper sparse layers and greedy search across dense bottom layers to balance query latency with recall accuracy
Vectorizing cosine similarity and L2 Euclidean distance computations using NumPy array operations to achieve sub-6ms query latency on single-core CPU
Implementing compact binary disk persistence for multi-million edge graph adjacency lists and fast memory-mapped index reloading
screener_signals: Clean Python repository implementing HNSW graph data structures, distance functions, index builders, and FastAPI endpoints from first principles
Algorithmic benchmark report proving >= 95% Recall@10 against exact brute-force ground truth on a 100,000 vector corpus (128-dimensional)
Anti-fake verification script querying a known synthetic outlier vector with deterministic nearest neighbors and asserting exact rank-order recall parity

architecture.data_flow: A client sends an embedding vector via FastAPI `/search`; the API parses query vector and parameters (K, ef_search); the search engine starts at the top-layer entry point of the HNSW graph; greedy search traverses down through sparse layers finding closest local minima; at layer 0, beam search evaluates candidates in a priority queue using NumPy cosine similarity; the top-K nearest vector IDs and similarity scores are returned to the client; on vector insertion (`/insert`), a random layer is assigned via exponential distribution; the graph connects the new vector to M neighbors per layer using heuristic pruning; periodic persistence writes graph state to disk.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: Exact mathematical cosine distance assertions and ground truth comparison against numpy.linalg brute-force matrix multiplication.

Understanding of linear algebra, high-dimensional vector spaces, distance metrics, and approximate nearest neighbor concepts

environment.gpu: None required (purely CPU bound NumPy vectorized numerical linear algebra)
environment.cost: $0 (fully open-source stack using local Python and Docker Desktop)
environment.accounts_keys_quotas: No external cloud API keys, paid vector database accounts (Pinecone/Weaviate), or managed services required

riskiest_component.name: Severe Recall Degradation from Poor Upper-Layer Graph Connectivity
riskiest_component.mitigation: Enforce minimum degree constraints on layer-0 entry points and apply heuristic neighbor selection favoring diverse angles.
riskiest_component.fallback: Automatic fallback to larger ef_search candidate pools if recall falls below 90% threshold.
